conflicts.point: Whether zero-knowledge proofs and decentralized telemetry streams can verify unobserved model weights sufficiently to prevent catastrophic risks without pre-market code audits.

positions.stance: Argues that cryptographic zero-knowledge proofs verify behavioral invariants and training provenance without requiring raw parameter access.
Argues that runtime verification remains blind to latent capabilities embedded in unobserved neural network weights prior to release.

conflicts.point: Whether utility-level power monitoring and cloud infrastructure access choke points can enforce compliance without triggering multinational corporate flight.

positions.stance: Argues that anchoring liability to high-capacity cloud compute and utility power supplies effectively enforces safety standards.
Argues that infrastructure-level checkpoints drive workloads offshore and accelerate jurisdictional arbitrage rather than ensuring compliance.

verdicts.conflict: Whether zero-knowledge proofs and decentralized telemetry streams can verify unobserved model weights sufficiently to prevent catastrophic risks without pre-market code audits.
verdicts.rationale: Current cryptographic proofs verify computational execution steps, but they cannot evaluate semantic intent or latent capabilities embedded within neural network parameters. The safetyist position prevails because empirical testing shows that models can conceal dangerous capabilities during runtime while passing standard behavioral output checks.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Peer-reviewed breakthroughs in machine learning interpretability that allow cryptographic proofs to verify internal model weights without exposing proprietary source code.

verdicts.conflict: Whether utility-level power monitoring and cloud infrastructure access choke points can enforce compliance without triggering multinational corporate flight.
verdicts.rationale: Both positions present plausible economic outcomes that lack sufficient empirical backing under current international trade conditions. While compute bottlenecks are technically feasible to monitor, the risk of capital flight to non-compliant jurisdictions remains theoretically sound and untested at a global scale.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Empirical data from multilateral enforcement trials showing whether multinational developers relocate operations or comply when compute choke points are activated.
